target_customer: Consumers booking on-demand hair and makeup at home, including working parents, professionals and men's grooming
problem: Salon appointments are hard to get and do not make house calls. StyleBee dispatched vetted beauty professionals through an app.
business_model: Marketplace with a take rate on bookings

founders.name: Anna Santeramo
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says she was a corporate attorney who started StyleBee after struggling to get hair appointments.

exit.reason: No shutdown announcement found; PitchBook lists Out of Business and YC lists Inactive.

competitors.name: Glamsquad
competitors.what: New York on-demand hair, makeup and nail service

competitors.name: Priv
competitors.what: On-demand beauty and wellness services marketplace, founded 2014

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking and dispatch marketplace app is standard engineering; the hard part is supply quality and scheduling.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded rivals offered the same service and professionals could work on many platforms, so copying was easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Consolidation occurred among rivals (Priv later merged with BeGlammed), but no source shows anyone buying StyleBee.

market_need_then: The YC post cites the founder's own difficulty getting hair appointments. Rival Glamsquad raised 7 million in October 2014 and 15 million in a Series B in October 2015, which shows investor appetite.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned in press as the Uber for hairstyling

branding.brand_signature: Uber for hairstyling positioning in VentureBeat

brand_strength.rationale: VentureBeat and TechCrunch covered it and the name is easy to say, but no evidence of logo, mascot, merch or community was found.

outcome_analysis: StyleBee joined YC Summer 2015, launched its app in July 2015 and operated a beauty marketplace in several cities against well funded rivals such as Glamsquad. It is now listed as out of business, but no source gives a date or cause, so the cause of failure is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: YC lists no website, so there was no site to fetch. The VentureBeat page fetch was rate limited, so its claim of 1 million raised including Y Combinator comes from a search snippet and is treated as a cumulative figure, not a single round. CB Insights shows 260K total with a 120K seed dated July 22, 2015 (single database); PitchBook says 377K; one snippet names Shervin Pishevar of Sherpa Ventures as an investor in an undated source, so it is not recorded. Founded year is unclear (sources say 2009, 2011 and a January 2014 TechCrunch article exists). Priv source is dated about three months after the batch. YC lists team size 11.
